overview.project_context: The Clockwork Vault is a solo adventure set inside a sealed ancient machine complex. Guided by Custodian Vex, the player restores four connected systems—Resonance Engine, Broken Gallery, Warden Halls, and the Great Orrery—so the century-sealed gateway can reopen. The journey focuses on learning invented rules, recovering from readable setbacks, and seeing the vault visibly return to life.
overview.main_experience: A solo restoration journey where the player learns invented vault mechanics, adapts to controlled setbacks, and restores the Great Orrery across four scored objectives.
overview.document_scope: Defines the complete player journey plus the level-design, runtime, scoring evidence, persistence, reset, and handoff requirements needed to build The Clockwork Vault.
overview.intended_use: Production reference for Level Design, Development, QA, and project review.

gameplay_flow.title: The Journey Begins
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The player discovers the Clockwork Vault beneath forgotten ruins and crosses its entrance before understanding that the gateway opens only once every hundred years.

beats.title: From Forgotten Ruins to the Sealed Vault
beats.description: The player discovers the Clockwork Vault beneath forgotten ruins and crosses its ancient entrance. The gate immediately seals behind them, trapping the player inside a place caught in a century-long restoration cycle. In the Antechamber, Custodian Vex awakens and explains that the vault was not built to hide treasure; it was built to protect the Great Orrery. The machine has been dormant for centuries, and the entrance cannot reopen until its connected mechanisms are restored in sequence.

beats.title: The Custodian’s Warning
beats.description: Custodian Vex explains that previous visitors attempted the same journey but never restored the full system. Every chamber controls a necessary part of the vault: power distribution, access through the collapsed inner gallery, the ancient security halls, and the final network feeding the Great Orrery. The player must proceed because no other exit exists.

beats.title: Beginning the Restoration
beats.description: The journey then proceeds through four gameplay objectives—Resonance Engine, Broken Gallery, Warden Halls, and Gremlin’s Workshop—before the restored Orrery opens the ending sequence.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: Vex directs the player to the central pedestal. Taking the Custodian Key activates the first seal and reveals the entrance to the Resonance Engine. From this point forward, every completed objective visibly awakens another section of the vault.

gameplay_flow.title: The Antechamber
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Antechamber is a protected lobby and narrative introduction where the player first meets Custodian Vex.

beats.title: Discovering the Clockwork Vault
beats.description: The Antechamber is a protected lobby and narrative introduction where the player first meets Custodian Vex. The room establishes the vault’s history, the century-sealed entrance, the failure of the Great Orrery, and the only possible route to freedom. The player is not tested here; the purpose is to establish motivation and make the complete journey understandable before Objective 1 begins.

beats.title: Receiving the Custodian Key
beats.description: A central pedestal holds the Custodian Key. Vex explains that the key is not the exit key; it grants access to the first mechanism that must be restored. The pedestal, the sealed entrance behind the player, and the Objective 1 gate must remain visible within the same composition so the player understands where they came from and where they must go.

beats.title: Opening the First Objective
beats.description: After the briefing, the player takes the Custodian Key from the central pedestal and uses it on the Resonance Engine seal. The keyed gate opens and hands control directly into Objective 1.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: When the player takes the Custodian Key and uses it on the first vault seal, the Resonance Engine door opens. Vex gives a concise objective briefing and the story moves from mystery into action.

gameplay_flow.title: The Resonance Engine
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The player enters a compact puzzle chamber with six levers, one pressure-plate submission, three crystal outputs, a physically visible but initially blank target display, and authored clue books.

beats.title: Free Experimentation
description: The player enters with all machine elements visible. Vex demonstrates that the levers and pressure plate are safe to use without revealing the hidden mapping. The target display is present but remains blank/inactive.

For approximately 90 seconds of game-time, the player can read clues and test inputs freely. Every valid interaction produces immediate crystal light/sound feedback and the complete panel state remains readable.

beats.title: Target 1 Appears
beats.description: After the free-play phase, Target 1 appears with a clear chime. The player compares the required Dark, Glowing, and Pulsing states with the observed machine behavior, adjusts the six lever configuration, and submits using the pressure plate. Incorrect submissions stay visible and can be revised immediately.

beats.title: Target 2 Requires the Learned Rule
beats.description: When Target 1 is confirmed, Target 2 appears. The second target must require the player to apply the distinguishing rule learned from clues/experimentation rather than repeat the first configuration. The objective remains recoverable until confirmation or the station deadline.

beats.title: Restoring the Resonance Engine
beats.description: Target 2 confirmation locks the completed Engine state, records the raw input/state and target timing evidence, activates the vault response, and opens the Broken Gallery transition. The platform calculates the Objective Score; the map does not display or export it.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The Broken Gallery opens after Target 2 confirmation and the Resonance Engine boundary record is secured.

gameplay_flow.title: The Broken Gallery
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The player enters a vast collapsed gallery with three route families: upper, lower, and side.

beats.title: Checkpoint 1 — Choosing a Viable Route
beats.description: The player enters a vast collapsed gallery with three route families: upper, lower, and side. None is fully intact. Building materials are collected near the starting checkpoint and must be used to repair gaps, missing stairs, broken ladders, or disconnected platforms. During Phase 1, two routes are valid and can reach Checkpoint 1, allowing the player to compare route readability and material cost.

beats.title: Phase 2 — Finding the Single Correct Continuation
beats.description: After Checkpoint 1, the gallery narrows into another three-route decision, but only one route can be completed with the available materials. The other routes provide visible warning signs and consume resources if chosen carelessly. The player must inspect the damage, estimate the required repairs, and commit before exhausting the limited kit. Checkpoint 2 secures progress and provides the final controlled material allocation.

beats.title: Checkpoint 3 — Crossing Before the Route Collapses
beats.description: Beyond Checkpoint 2, the final crossing becomes unstable. A visible warning sequence starts, and the player must move efficiently through the authored repairs. Around 50% of Checkpoint 3 progress, the current segment resolves into its collapsed/sealed state from a safe event position. The player then uses the remaining recovery connector/route to continue. Failure or a fall returns the player to the nearest valid checkpoint/ledge with the final-phase state recoverable; the full objective does not restart.

beats.title: Placing the Custodian Key
beats.description: After the recovery crossing, the player reaches the far pedestal and places the Custodian Key. The Gallery records checkpoint progress, resource state, collapse response, resupply use, and completion before opening the Warden Halls.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The Warden Halls open after the Custodian Key is accepted by the far pedestal and the Gallery completion record is secured.

gameplay_flow.title: The Warden Halls
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The Warden Halls are a controlled security corridor containing wall sensors, floor traps, and ceiling traps.

beats.title: Phase 1 — Learning the Three Trap Families
beats.description: The Warden Halls are a controlled security corridor containing wall sensors, floor traps, and ceiling traps. Each type has a distinct silhouette, warning cue, active state, and non-lethal consequence. The player receives an Echo Pebble that can disable wall and floor traps for a 4-second game-time window. Ceiling traps cannot be disabled and must be passed through observation and timing.

beats.title: Phase 2 — Combining Trap Types
beats.description: After the first checkpoint, wall, floor, and ceiling hazards begin appearing in combinations. Echo Pebble use creates a 4-second safe window on valid wall/floor targets, so the player must disable the correct trap, read the remaining active hazard, and move before the disabled trap recovers. Failure costs time or returns the player to the nearest safe checkpoint.

beats.title: Phase 3 — Crossing the Final Security Sequence
beats.description: The final phase uses denser combinations and shorter decision windows while preserving the same established rules. The player must choose when to use the Echo Pebble, when to wait, and when to move through an unavoidable ceiling cycle. The difficulty increases through composition, not by introducing unexplained trap behavior.

beats.title: Reaching the Inner Vault
beats.description: After the final trap sequence, the player reaches the protected Records Room. The hall completion state is recorded and the route toward Gremlin’s Workshop opens.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: After the final trap sequence, the player reaches the inner gate and the entrance to the Gremlin’s Workshop. Vex confirms that the Wardens never stopped protecting the Orrery; the still-active defence system proves that the vault has continued performing its purpose throughout the centuries.
gameplay_flow.eyebrow: Phase 1 — Learning the Three Trap Families

gameplay_flow.title: The Gremlin’s Workshop
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: The final chamber contains the Source Crystal, the Great Orrery, three target rings, and a 3×3 grid of rotatable conduit nodes.

beats.title: Connecting Ring 1
beats.description: The final chamber contains the Source Crystal, the Great Orrery, three target rings, and a 3×3 grid of rotatable conduit nodes. Every conduit has visible connection sides and rotates in 90-degree steps. Power travels only through sides that physically connect. The player first creates one valid route from the Source Crystal to Ring 1.

beats.title: Connecting Ring 2 and Surviving the Sabotage
beats.description: Ring 2 must be connected while Ring 1 remains powered, requiring the player to build a cumulative network rather than replace the first solution. After Ring 2 stabilizes, a Gremlin visibly crosses the board and destroys one active conduit connection between the Source Crystal and an already powered ring. The damaged connection is permanently marked and cannot conduct power again during the run.

beats.title: Rebuilding and Extending the Network
beats.description: The sabotage interrupts the active network. The player must rotate the remaining conduits to establish a new valid route from the Source Crystal, restore the disconnected ring, preserve the other active ring, and then extend the network to Ring 3. The final challenge is therefore not a reversed pipe rule; it is a cumulative rerouting problem with one known connection permanently unavailable.

beats.title: Restoring the Great Orrery
beats.description: When all three rings are powered at the same time, the Great Orrery enters its restored state. Puzzle input closes and the controlled Vault Restored ending begins.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The objective completes only when Ring 1, Ring 2, and Ring 3 are powered simultaneously. The Great Orrery begins rotating, energy returns throughout the vault, and the ending sequence starts. If the player reaches the configured assist threshold, Vex may highlight a valid connection without rotating the board automatically; the player still completes the route.

gameplay_flow.title: The Vault Awakens
gameplay_flow.narrative_context: When all three rings remain powered, the Great Orrery begins turning for the first time in centuries.

beats.title: Awakening the Great Orrery
beats.description: When all three rings remain powered, the Great Orrery begins turning for the first time in centuries. Energy travels backward through every completed chamber: the Resonance crystals synchronize, gallery guide lights return, the Warden systems enter standby, and the century-sealed entrance begins unlocking. The ending visually confirms that the player restored one connected machine rather than completing unrelated challenges.

beats.title: Resolving the Custodian’s Story
beats.description: Custodian Vex thanks the player and acknowledges that the vault was never waiting for someone merely to escape; it was waiting for someone capable of restoring it. The player receives the Clockwork Wayfinder reward after the completion record has been saved.

beats.title: Leaving the Clockwork Vault
beats.description: After the result and Clockwork Wayfinder reward state are secured, the player follows the safe return route to the Holding Area while the assigned lane begins cleanup and reset.

gameplay_flow.next_destination: The player exits through the reopened gateway as the Great Orrery continues operating behind them. The entrance closes gradually, not as another trap, but as the vault returns to its century-long cycle with its purpose restored. Temporary gameplay state is then cleared and the assigned lane is prepared for reuse.

global_development.overview: Build one isolated Clockwork journey per active player lane. Shared runtime systems own session start, transitions, pause, data, interruption, and reset, while each objective owns its local mechanic and completion state.

items.title: Lane Architecture
details: Use one player per lane and five station cells plus ending space.
Prevent visual, audio, entity, particle, and state leakage between lanes.
Start the session only when the player exits the holding-area gate.
items.result: Defines safe parallel ownership for school sessions.

items.title: Story and Navigation
details: Keep fixed order: Antechamber → Resonance → Gallery → Warden → Workshop → Ending.
Use one-way corridors for briefing, cleanup, boundary save, and next-station activation.
items.result: Maintains one coherent adventure and clean state boundaries.

items.title: Deterministic Treatment
details: Use authored template/layout selection and fixed event dose.
Do not randomize collapse, traps, fault timing, or rule effects at runtime.
items.result: Keeps player conditions comparable and verifiable.

items.title: Input and Accessibility
details: Support keyboard, controller, and touch equally.
Use simple interactions, no combat, no death, no precision parkour, and no vanilla-knowledge dependency.
items.result: Preserves the target experience for students aged 9–14.

items.title: Data and Scoring Boundary
details: Emit raw timestamped events only.
Provide enough evidence for platform-side objective scoring without showing or sending final score from the map.
items.result: Separates gameplay implementation from platform interpretation.

items.title: Reset and Readiness
details: Reset every lane in under 30 seconds.
Test pause, interruption, rejoin, timeout, completion, multi-lane load, and no-leakage behavior.
items.result: Makes the map ready for back-to-back use.

notes.title: Lane Isolation
notes.description: Every active player owns one isolated lane; visual, audio, entity, particle, and gameplay state must not leak between lanes.

notes.title: Deterministic Objectives
notes.description: Authored targets, trap cycles, collapse behavior, and Gremlin sabotage remain reproducible across equivalent lanes.

notes.title: Score Boundary

notes.description: A lane returns to service only after objective, ending, inventory, entity, timing, and temporary-block state are verified clean.

global_development.title: Game System
global_development.subtitle: Sessions, ownership, and objective control
global_development.overview: The shared runtime controls lane ownership, objective order, Custodian Vex, game-time, pause, inventory, permissions, transitions, and interruption handling. Objective mechanics plug into this lifecycle without changing its global rules.

flow.title: Session and Lane Setup
flow.description: Assign one player, initialize lane ownership, and keep the holding area isolated until the start gate.

flow.title: Station Lifecycle
flow.description: Run briefing → active → complete/timeout/interrupted → transition with one authoritative station state.

flow.title: Pause and Persistence
flow.description: Freeze game-time, player input, and scheduled events; save every boundary and interruption.

flow.title: Ending and Release
flow.description: Complete the session, deliver reward/data, return to lobby, and release the lane only after reset verification.

items.title: Holding Area and Start
details: Contain players until they use the start gate.
Start master/session game-time only after lane entry.
Prevent early visibility of active stations.
items.result: Absorbs uneven classroom joins without shortening gameplay.

items.title: Lane Isolation
details: Own players, entities, effects, sounds, particles, scoreboards, timers, and temporary blocks by lane.
Reject cross-lane interaction and clean lane-owned objects at every boundary.
items.result: Prevents another player’s event from spoiling or changing the experience.

items.title: Custodian Vex
details: Use one persistent guide per lane with short externalized dialogue.
Pair every instruction with demonstration or highlight.
Do not reveal hidden rules before experimentation.
items.result: Provides instruction, tone, and blameless setback reactions.

items.title: Inventory and Permissions
details: Clear and grant station-specific inventory at entry.
Apply scripted break/place/interact permissions only to current station targets.
Remove permissions/items at exit, interruption, and reset.
items.result: Prevents map damage and cross-station state leakage.

items.title: Game-Time and Pause
details: Own all timers and scheduled events in script game-time.
Pause player/camera input, timers, trap cycles, collapse, and fault at exact state.
Keep absolute session hard caps according to the approved session rule.
items.result: Makes pause deterministic without real-time drift.

items.title: Setback Feedback
details: Use telegraph → impact → Vex reaction for Gallery collapse, trap consequences, and Gremlin fault.
Ensure visual treatment carries meaning when audio is muted.
items.result: Makes external setbacks readable and memorable.

items.title: Boundary and Transition
details: Save station data, clear temporary state, close the previous route, brief the next station, and activate only after entry is safe.
Complete, timeout, and interruption must use distinct exit reasons.
items.result: Creates reliable station boundaries.

items.title: Rejoin Behavior
details: Save partial data immediately on disconnect.
Mark station interrupted and restart that station from initial state on rejoin while preserving completed objective results.
items.result: Protects data without resuming into an invalid temporary state.

notes.title: Script-Owned Timing
notes.description: Use Script API / scoreboard-owned timing rather than redstone clocks for objective lifecycle and scheduled events.

notes.title: Fixed Authored Rules
notes.description: Adaptive tiering does not rewrite Clockwork puzzle or hazard rules in this version.

notes.title: Localization Ready
notes.description: Keep in-game strings externalized so localized copy can be added without changing gameplay logic.

notes.title: Concurrent Lane Test
notes.description: Shared systems must remain isolated and stable with all supported lanes active together.

global_development.title: Data and Reset
global_development.subtitle: Timing, valid results, interruptions, and arena recovery
global_development.overview: Each objective records the raw gameplay events needed to reconstruct its result. Data is saved at objective boundaries and interruptions; the assigned lane is released only after temporary state is cleared, authored structures are restored, and readiness checks pass.

flow.title: Capture
flow.description: Record session, station, action, state, dose, pause, completion, timeout, and interruption events.

flow.title: Persist and Send
flow.description: Buffer safely, save at boundaries, and retry delivery without duplicate semantic events.

flow.title: Clear Runtime State
flow.description: Remove inventory, permissions, entities, particles, scheduled tasks, temporary blocks, and lane properties.

flow.title: Restore and Verify
flow.description: Reload structures, restore defaults, run readiness checks, then release the lane.

items.title: Common Envelope
details: Every event carries anonymous session ID, map ID, station ID, lane ID, build version, event name, and game-time timestamp.
Do not send player name, gamertag, device identifier, platform interpretation, or final map-side score.
items.result: Provides consistent anonymous event ownership.

items.title: Objective Payloads
details: Record the exact action and complete resulting state needed to reconstruct Resonance and Workshop behavior.
Record route/resource, trap/strategy, event dose, pause, completion, timeout, and interruption fields where required.
items.result: Provides platform scoring evidence without aggregation in-world.

items.title: Boundary Save
details: Save and send at station exit, disconnect, ending, and session end.
Use idempotent event IDs or sequence numbers to prevent duplicate delivery after retry.
items.result: Prevents loss and duplication.

items.title: Timing Rules
details: Use game-time timestamps; pause freezes gameplay timing.
Record scripted event dose exactly, including route collapsed, trap instance, and connection sabotaged.
items.result: Allows fair timing and treatment verification.

items.title: Script Cleanup
details: Cancel scheduled callbacks; clear station state, UI, effects, entities, items, permissions, scoreboards, and lane dynamic properties.
Remove any player-placed or temporary blocks before structure restore.
items.result: Prevents stale runtime logic.

items.title: Structure Restore and Verification
details: Restore all station cells and ending states from approved structures.
Verify doors, targets, items, guide, timers, event flags, chosen variants, and player state.
Release lane only after all readiness checks pass within 30 seconds.
items.result: Guarantees pristine reuse.

items.title: Interrupted Sessions
details: Preserve partial data and mark incomplete.
On rejoin, restart the interrupted station and retain earlier completed objective results.
items.result: Protects evidence while avoiding corrupted temporary state.

items.title: Delivery or Reset Failure
details: Queue failed data sends for retry and keep semantic IDs stable.
Keep a lane unavailable when reset verification fails and surface a technical error for staff.
items.result: Prevents silent data loss and unsafe reuse.

notes.title: Objective-Owned Payloads
notes.description: Each objective emits only the raw fields needed to reconstruct its gameplay result and treatment state.

notes.title: Raw Data Stays Raw
notes.description: Platform scoring or interpretation never changes the event payload produced by the map.

items.title: Activation and Ownership

Restore authored structures and initial mechanic state.

gameplay.context: The player enters the protected Antechamber and meets Custodian Vex. A central pedestal holds the Custodian Key, and the Resonance Engine seal is the visible next destination.
gameplay.main_objective: Listen to Vex’s briefing, collect the Custodian Key, and use it on the Resonance Engine seal.
gameplay.result: The seal opens and the Resonance Engine becomes accessible. The Antechamber creates no Objective Score.
gameplay.purpose: Establish story, navigation, pickup/use interaction, and the next destination without adding a separate warm-up minigame.
gameplay.start_condition: The player leaves the holding area in Adventure mode with the assigned lane active and the Antechamber reset.
gameplay.end_condition: The Custodian Key is accepted by the Resonance Engine seal and the objective door opens.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: There is no lethal or permanent fail state. If the key interaction is missed or interrupted, Vex repeats the cue and the key/seal state remains recoverable.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: No Objective Score. Completion is recorded as story progression only.

packages.title: The Broken Gallery

gameplay.context: The player enters a ruined three-checkpoint crossing with upper, lower, and side route variations. A fixed construction kit is granted at the start.
gameplay.main_objective: Carry the Custodian Key across all three checkpoints. In Checkpoint 3, adapt to the scripted collapse and reach the far pedestal through the valid recovery path.

gameplay.end_condition: The Custodian Key is accepted by the far pedestal after the player clears Checkpoint 3.

packages.title: The Gremlin’s Workshop

gameplay.context: The Workshop contains the Source Crystal, a 3×3 rotatable conduit grid, and the three-ring Great Orrery. After Ring 2, a Gremlin permanently breaks one active connection and the player must reroute around it.
gameplay.main_objective: Power Ring 1 and Ring 2, recover from the scripted sabotage, then reroute the network to power Ring 3 while restoring the full Orrery network.
gameplay.result: All three rings are powered together, the Great Orrery is restored, and the ending sequence begins.
gameplay.purpose: Test cumulative power-routing understanding and adaptation to a visible topology change rather than a hidden rule reversal.
gameplay.start_condition: The 3×3 grid is reset, all three ring targets are visible, Ring 1 has its easy authored route, and no connection is sabotaged.
gameplay.end_condition: All three Orrery rings are powered simultaneously after the post-sabotage reroute.
gameplay.blocked_or_fail_condition: No permanent fail state. Rotations remain reversible; the sabotaged connection stays broken, but a valid authored reroute always exists. Vex may highlight a useful area but never solve the board.
gameplay.scoring_criteria: Objective Score 0–100 based on Ring Completion, Post-Fault Adaptation, and Independent Progress.

Show the broken connection as a physical topology change.

items.title: Scripted Connection Sabotage

Record the broken edge ID, prior flow state, fault time, and first post-fault interaction. Keep all normal conduit connection rules unchanged.
items.result: Creates one clear external topology change identical for every session.

items.title: Ring 3 Reroute
details: Recalculate the network with the broken edge unavailable.
Require the player to restore any lost powered segment by using an authored alternate route and then extend valid power to Ring 3.
Complete only when all three rings are simultaneously powered.
items.result: Verifies real adaptation to the broken network.
